messages:
nina: heads-up — started seeing a p99 latency jump ~03:12 UTC on a few hosts serving long-context streams. p95 mild, p99 spiking to ~350ms from ~30ms. correlates with KV cache churn. filing here as I dig.

mike: which hosts / can you drop a sample span? any common model or kernel selection change rolled?

nina: 3 hosts in us-west-2, same runtime build, no kernel change. model variant is opt-4x-q4. batching heuristics unchanged. I grabbed traces and a small flamegraph: https://internal/fg/4109998887 (private).

oliver: ping @mike @sara — saw anything on the evicter? I saw increased pagewalks in the pager logs earlier.

mike: looking now. quick grep: evicter events increased ~4x at 03:11:58.

ben: paste of the evicter log snippet I pulled:
```
[03:11:57.942] evicter: start_scan slab=12 entries=32768 free=1024
[03:11:57.945] evicter: evicted=4096 reuse_hits=128 reclaim_ms=42
[03:11:58.101] pager: page_in miss_count=4128 io_ms=30
```

ben: memory growth over the stream session: resident rose from 2.1GB -> 3.6GB over ~6 minutes on one host.

sara: interesting — reuse_hits low while evicted high. suggests fragmentation (many small disjoint slices) or FIFO path stealing recently-wounded entries. can you repro with a synthetic long-context workload?

nina: repro script attached (ran locally): `./tools/kv-long-context -concurrency 8 -len 64k -pattern churn` reproduced p99 spike.

oliver: I perf profiled while reproducing. top symbols: evicter::scan 42%, kv::reclaim 22%, pager::page_in 12%. sample from perf:
```
#00 evicter::scan
#01 kv::touch_or_reinsert
#02 memcpy
```

mike: two theories: (1) LRU bookkeeping under sustained inserts causes cache-walk hot loop (pathological access pattern); (2) FIFO reinserts create chain re-traversal causing fragmentation and extra page faults.

sara: code excerpt — current reinsertion path (simplified):
```
if (policy==FIFO) {
  slab.append(entry) // O(1)
} else { // LRU
  list.move_to_head(entry) // O(1) but touching neighbors
}
```
Potentially the O(1) is hiding cache-line thrash when many concurrent threads touch slab metadata.

ben: i ran a run toggling policy to LRU-only on one host. result: p99 improved to ~80ms but CPU on main thread increased. memory reclaim rate lower. So LRU reduces page_in but higher CPU.

nina: important: we must also check correctness — there were 2 reports of transient not-found for entries being streamed. could be a race during reinsertion/paging. anyone saw errors?

mike: I saw a WARN: "kv: attempted access to tombstoned entry" in one trace. attaching small stack: kv::get -> kv::touch -> tombstone_check.

oliver: that might be a double-free / race between evicter and request path. under pressure the evicter reclaims while touch is racing to reinsert. We may be missing a refcount window.

sara: quick mitigation: introduce a short grace window before reclaiming recently touched entries (microseconds). experiment: bump probation window from 5ms -> 50ms.

ben: did the bump. p99 dropped to ~120ms and tombstone WARN disappeared on the test host. but throughput slightly lower.

nina: nice. any profiling showing reduced pagewalks?

oliver: yes — evicter scans decreased ~30% and page_in rate halved. flamegraph deeper shows fewer memcpy spikes.

mike: longer-term: two path fixes: (A) strengthen the touch/reinsert atomicity (refcounts + CAS) to prevent ephemeral tombstones, (B) adaptive policy: prefer LRU under long-context workloads, prefer FIFO for short-lifespan workloads. we can wire workload signal from routing.

sara: also consider batching evict ops off hot request threads onto a dedicated evicter worker to reduce metadata thrash. that decouples reclaim latency from request latency.

nina: action items:
- mike: prototype refcount guard + CAS by EOD (feature branch kv/evict-refcount)
- oliver: test adaptive policy heuristics with synthetic client (long vs short) — measure p99 + cpu tradeoffs
- ben: run cluster-wide probation-window bump rollout (canary 5 hosts) and monitor tombstone WARNs and page_in rates
- sara: spec design doc for decoupled evicter worker + API for workload hinting (short doc pls)

ci-bot: deployment queued for canary hosts: kv-probation-bump-50ms -> canary(5) -> monitor(30m). Link: https://ci/repo/kv/commits/6a7f2

nina: thanks all — will follow up with the traces and perf captures. progress looks promising :thumbsup:
